definitions: Relating to or denoting the actions of a body that has powers resembling those of a court of law but is not a court itself.

Having a partly judicial character by possession of the right to hold hearings on and conduct investigations into disputed claims and alleged infractions of rules and to make decisions in the manner of a court.
examples: The board's quasi-judicial functions include hearing appeals.
Many administrative agencies have quasi-judicial authority.
The tribunal operates in a quasi-judicial capacity.
